cim: ‘Mormon Land’: Should you confess your sins to A.I.? Some Latter-day Saints say yes.
cim_eredeti: ‘Mormon Land’: Should you confess your sins to A.I.? Some Latter-day Saints say yes.
szoveg_eredeti:
(The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints) Apostle Gerrit W. Gong speaks about artificial intelligence to church employees in 2024.

Since at least 2024, leaders of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints have been warning members against treating artificial intelligence as God.

“A.I. cannot provide inspired divine truth or independent moral guidance,” apostle Gerrit W. Gong told audiences in an August 2025 presentation at church-owned Brigham Young University’s Education Week.

Elsewhere, the church has discouraged members from using it to write talks and otherwise shortcut the work needed for spiritual growth.

This was the question that inspired a new study on Latter-day Saint views of A.I. and data centers. Conducted in 2025 and 2026, the survey included nearly 1,800 self-identified members from across the U.S.

On this week’s show, two of its co-authors — Matthew Miles, a professor of political science at BYU–Idaho, and Peter Cardon, a professor of business communication at the University of Southern California — discuss their findings.

(Matthew Miles, Peter Cardon) Researchers Matthew Miles, left, and Peter Cardon are two of three co-authors of a new study examining Latter-day Saint attitudes around artificial intelligence.
